## 14. Decision rule (evaluated EXACTLY ONCE)

Mechanical evaluator: intel/experiments/unbrowse_ladder_multihost/
evaluate_rule.py (frozen hash below) reading ONLY committed evidence under
results/intel/reproductions/cycle6/.

Invalidity conditions (any => MEASUREMENT_INVALID): required evidence files
missing/unparseable; fewer than 4/5 P0 host probes up; >1 host-task with <3
valid A/B pairs; mutation schedule_hash_verified != True.

Clauses:
- C1 multi-host discovery fidelity: for EACH of the 4 host-tasks both genuine
  discovery completions accepted AND >=1 route learned AND discovery-time
  replay REPLAY_OK at acceptance-equivalence. PASS iff 4/4.
- C2 replay economics: per task >=3 valid pairs, median speedup(A/B) >= 2.0,
  BCa log-ratio ci_low > 0, B actions==0 < A actions, B equivalence on all
  valid pairs; PLUS family gates: all four Holm-adjusted sign p<0.05 AND
  leave-one-host-out directional stability. PASS iff all 4 tasks.
- C3 capture-value-over-declaration: demoblaze B success rate >= 0.9 over its
  30 measured passes AND demoblaze D success rate <= 0.4 over 5 passes.
- C4 mutation detection (replica-scoped): hash verified; M1/M2/M3/M5/M6 all
  detected; 0/25 benign false positives (Wilson upper <= 0.15); pristine
  rechecks all OK. M4 blind-excluded.
- C5 lifecycle core: RB independent checker all_pass (Q1 parameterization to
  two NEW ids field-equal vs direct ground truth; Q2 corrupted-auth =>
  AUTH_FAIL with nothing presented + positive control round-trip; Q3 rewind
  compliance; Q4 deleted record surfaced as HTTP_ERROR 404 absence; pointer-
  only store assertion).

Verdict mapping (mechanical):
- invalidity condition => MEASUREMENT_INVALID
- !C1 => FAILED_TO_REPRODUCE (multi-host capture->extract->parameterize->
  replay effect absent)
- C1 & C2 & C3 & C4 & C5 => REPRODUCED_USEFUL
- C1 & !C2 & !C3 => REPRODUCED_NO_ADVANTAGE (routes learned but no operational
  advantage attributable to the abstraction over declaration/raw HTTP)
- else => INCONCLUSIVE (partial pattern not covered above; per-clause table
  reported honestly)

Natural-TTL never enters the verdict (withheld, §13). Wording ceilings:
mutation claims replica-scoped only; economics claims UI-traversal-vs-direct-
HTTP under scripted policies only; hand-authored addressing ground truth
disclosed; vendor 94-domain headline remains OFFICIAL_CLAIM regardless of
outcome; PROOF OF CONCEPT ceiling maximum (scripted policies, sandbox scope,
n small, no LLM agents, no shared-graph tier, HTML tier out of scope).

BCa fallback (mechanically defined): `stats.bca_or_percentile` falls back
to plain percentile bootstrap on the SAME deterministic resamples iff
fewer than 3 deltas, prop_lt in {0,1}, jackknife denominator < 1e-12, or
any non-finite intermediate; the method label is committed either way.

Pair-outcome semantics (frozen verbatim):
- valid pair: both A and B rows completed with payload_ok=true; win iff
  B_ms < A_ms else loss (B slower = LOSS).
- completed-but-lost: B row present, payload_ok=false, classified loss
  (SCHEMA_MISMATCH / AUTH_FAIL / STALE_TTL / HTTP_ERROR 4xx / accept
  false with no exception) - STAYS IN the sign-test denominator as a
  loss. A row completed-not-ok with no exception => environment-side
  exclusion of the pair, logged.
- harness/host-error exclusions: exception strings, codes
  {NO_ROUTE, PARAM_UNRESOLVED, ESCALATED_*}, HTTP_ERROR >=500/timeout -
  leave the denominator, logged with class counts.
Replacement policy: scheduled volume IS the oversampling buffer; there
are NO replacement attempts beyond schedule; a task ending below
n_valid=8 through exclusions yields honest component failure (family
gate evaluates mechanically; typically INCONCLUSIVE), NOT invalidity -
environment-side attrition is not an instrument failure.

C2' per-task component gates (ALL required): n_valid_pairs >= 8;
median warm-amortized speedup(A/B) >= 2.0 (warmups excluded; identical
to c7); bca_or_percentile log-ratio ci_low > 0; B actions == 0 on ALL B
rows; B equivalence on ALL valid pairs. Family: Holm-adjusted one-sided
sign p < 0.05 for ALL tasks AND leave-one-host-out directional stability
(median_B < median_A and wins >= 0.7n per exclusion; mechanic inherited).
Cold/warm reporting (descriptive, NO threshold): first-B-ever latency and
warm median per task committed in the evaluation output.

BCa fallback (mechanically defined): `stats.bca_or_percentile` falls back
to plain percentile bootstrap on the SAME deterministic resamples iff
fewer than 3 deltas, prop_lt in {0,1}, jackknife denominator < 1e-12, or
any non-finite intermediate; the method label is committed either way.

Pair-outcome semantics (frozen verbatim):
- valid pair: both A and B rows completed with payload_ok=true; win iff
  B_ms < A_ms else loss (B slower = LOSS).
- completed-but-lost: B row present, payload_ok=false, classified loss
  (SCHEMA_MISMATCH / AUTH_FAIL / STALE_TTL / HTTP_ERROR 4xx / accept
  false with no exception) - STAYS IN the sign-test denominator as a
  loss. A row completed-not-ok with no exception => environment-side
  exclusion of the pair, logged.
- harness/host-error exclusions: exception strings, codes
  {NO_ROUTE, PARAM_UNRESOLVED, ESCALATED_*}, HTTP_ERROR >=500/timeout -
  leave the denominator, logged with class counts.
Replacement policy: scheduled volume IS the oversampling buffer; there
are NO replacement attempts beyond schedule; a task ending below
n_valid=8 through exclusions yields honest component failure (family
gate evaluates mechanically; typically INCONCLUSIVE), NOT invalidity -
environment-side attrition is not an instrument failure.

C2' per-task component gates (ALL required): n_valid_pairs >= 8;
median warm-amortized speedup(A/B) >= 2.0 (warmups excluded; identical
to c7); bca_or_percentile log-ratio ci_low > 0; B actions == 0 on ALL B
rows; B equivalence on ALL valid pairs. Family: Holm-adjusted one-sided
sign p < 0.05 for ALL tasks AND leave-one-host-out directional stability
(median_B < median_A and wins >= 0.7n per exclusion; mechanic inherited).
Cold/warm reporting (descriptive, NO threshold): first-B-ever latency and
warm median per task committed in the evaluation output.

    "page_text": "Quotes to Scrape Login \u201cThe world as we have created it is a process of our thinking. It cannot be changed without changing our thinking.\u201d by Albert Einstein (about) Tags: change deep-thoughts thinking world \u201cIt is our choices, Harry, that show what we truly are, far more than our abilities.\u201d by J.K.     "n_links": 4,
    "page_text": "Dynamically Loaded Page Elements It's common to see an action get triggered that returns a result dynamically. It does not rely on the page to reload or finish loading. The page automatically gets updated (e.g. hiding elements, showing elements, updating copy, etc) through the use of JavaScript. There are two examples. One in which an element already exists on the page but it is not displayed. And anonther where the element is not on the page and gets added in. Example 1: Element on page that is hidden Example 2: Element rendered after the fact Powered by Elemental Selenium",

~~~
# CYCLE 6 REPAIR ROUND 2 — RESTORATION NOTE (RF-A)

Date: 2026-08-25
Run: 32897120087 (`intel-loop.yml`, cycle_index=6, repair_from_run_id=32890075186, repair_round=2)
Branch: `cycle/intel/32897120087/repro` (parent = accepted lane tip `8bfcf85`)
Restores: `origin/cycle/intel/32878215017/repro` @ `c1543f8` ("Intel cycle 6 repair 0: reproduction")
Precedent: cycle-1 repair round 3 documented byte-exact restoration
(`results/intel/reproductions/cycle1_repair3_restoration_note.md`).

## What was restored

All 18 instrumentation files under `intel/experiments/unbrowse_ladder_multihost/`
were restored from commit `c1543f8` via `git checkout c1543f8 -- <path>` and
verified byte-exact against the source commit's git blob hashes:

```
__init__.py addressing.py canon.py capture.py extract.py ladder.py pilot.py
probes_rb.py quiescence.py replay.py replica.py routestore.py run_all.py
schedule.py selftest.py specgen.py stats.py tasks_hosts.py
```

Verification method: `git rev-parse c1543f8:<path>` compared to
`git hash-object <restored file>` for all 18 files -> **18/18 identical**
(executed before any edit; transcript in the repair-round session log).

Offline re-verification after edits: `python3 -m
intel.experiments.unbrowse_ladder_multihost.selftest` -> **49/49 PASS**;
sealed schedule hash recomputed =
`276132df2f6a57a466d3b84d918e03acc177c10d2e82f745d028f9f02c4efbb8`
(matches the auditor-sealed value in gates CYCLE_32878215017 /
CYCLE_32890075186; schedule.py itself is UNEDITED).

## Code deltas vs c1543f8 (complete list)

Round-0 RF-2 / round-1 RF-B mandated "the sole code delta" be the baseline-arm
timing fix. During pre-freeze verification, two additional by-construction
measurement-validity defects and one ethics defect were identified in the
restored tree. Shipping them silently would have made the preregistered test
incapable of passing on the pivotal task regardless of the mechanism's actual
behavior (a guaranteed false negative), and one defect would have made hygiene
deletes touch other sessions' rows on a shared demo backend. Master-prompt
§24 ("code/data/report disagreement") and §33 ("A negative result can be just
as wrong as a positive result") govern: all three were repaired BEFORE the
freeze, are individually documented here and in the prereg, are mechanical,
and none was chosen or tuned after observing any condition-level outcome
(no confirmatory collection existed at edit time; the freeze commit precedes
all collection). If the auditor rejects any delta, the affected clause is
void, not reinterpreted.

### DELTA-1 (RF-B, mandated) — tasks_hosts.py::flow_demoblaze_cart
Removed `time.sleep(1.2)` from the TIMED arm-A region (cycle-2-forensics bias
class: additive constant in the comparator arm only). Replaced with
`_quiesce(tracker)` — the same observable-condition calibrated-quiescence wait
used after every other interaction in the same flow. No additive constant
remains; demoblaze arm A now carries zero fixed sleeps inside its timer.

### DELTA-2 (measurement-validity wiring) — run_all.py + tasks_hosts.py
`HOST_TASK_SPECS["T_DEMOBLAZE_CART"]["accept"]` is the BROWSER-side acceptance
(`target_found`/`target_price == 790`) while B/D project payloads via
`project_demoblaze_viewcart` -> `{n_entries, prod_ids_present}`. The existing
`accept_demoblaze_replay()` contract was defined but wired into NO call site,
so every B/D/P2 demoblaze equivalence check would have been False BY
CONSTRUCTION. Repair: spec declares `"accept_replay": accept_demoblaze_replay`;
run_B_pass / run_D_pass / P2 use `spec.get("accept_replay") or spec["accept"]`.
A-side acceptance untouched; all other tasks unaffected (no accept_replay key).
This TIGHTENS the test (makes the preregistered gate reachable); it does not
loosen any threshold.

### DELTA-3a (discovery first-party scope) — tasks_hosts.py HOST_TASK_SPECS
`T_DEMOBLAZE_CART["origin"]` changed `https://www.demoblaze.com` ->
`https://api.demoblaze.com`. The SPA's task traffic all targets
api.demoblaze.com; TrafficRecorder/is_candidate/har_to_spec filter strictly by
netloc equality, so with the UI host as origin every API body was rejected and
demoblaze discovery could learn ZERO routes by construction (the frozen
intent_map keys already name api.demoblaze.com URLs, proving design intent).
Browser flows still navigate to www.demoblaze.com; only the first-party filter
scope changed to the operator's actual API host. `host` (quiescence key)
unchanged.

### DELTA-3b (ethics: ownership-scoped cleanup) — tasks_hosts.py::DemoblazeSession.cleanup
Disclosed pre-freeze contract probe (/tmp/opencode/c6_pilot/
contract_probe_demoblaze.json, quoted in prereg) showed the shared demo
backend's /viewcart returns entries created by OTHER sessions (85 rows on a
fresh account) and the shipped cleanup deleted ALL of them. Repair: cleanup
now deletes ONLY entries whose `cookie` field equals our own session token.
Rows owned by other sessions are never touched.

### DELTA-4 (pre-outcome crash repair, appended post-freeze via prereg erratum E1)
First post-freeze launch crashed at P1 session bootstrap before any
observation existed: round-0 code two-value-unpacked the SINGLE dict returned
by HttpbinCookieSession.bootstrap() (iterating its keys). Caller fixed to
single assignment; bootstrap() unchanged. Disclosed in prereg ERRATUM
APPENDIX E1 with the aborted-attempt side effects (one throwaway demo account;
zero durable artifacts). run_all.py sha256 after DELTA-4:
07d2b3d3829cd23a59e46b8453dff0476b5fcbc89fcc9434812fe3bd5d78338e.

## Round-1 failure-mode structural exclusion

Round 1 failed because work never reached the durable tree. This round:
after the final commit, `git status` / `git diff 8bfcf85..HEAD --stat` must
show the restored+fixed code, the prereg, the raw evidence tree
`results/intel/reproductions/cycle6/`, this note, the report, and both updated
state files. Verified before finishing (see report §delivery).
~~~

# NON-EVIDENCE — PRE-FREEZE PROOF-PASS ARTIFACTS (cycle 7)

Everything in this directory is marked NON-EVIDENCE per the mission
stop-condition (b): the mechanical instrumentation proof-pass executed
BEFORE the cycle-7 preregistration freeze. None of these files is
confirmatory data; the frozen evaluator reads only the post-freeze evidence
under `results/intel/reproductions/cycle7/`.

- `proof_pass_report.json` — final clean proof-pass report (all eight gates
  PASS). Probe volume inside. Two earlier proof-pass executions surfaced
  three instrument findings; all were repaired BEFORE the second (clean)
  pass and BEFORE the freeze, and are disclosed in prereg section 11:
    1. P-ECHO widening: browser client-hint/trace fields (Sec-Ch-Ua*,
       X-Amzn-Trace-Id) absent from any fixed header list produced
       missing-key deviations on httpbin FORM smoke -> policy amended to
       strip ALL keys under a detected echo-envelope headers object.
    2. Proof-pass smoke harness bug: it passed empty params to a task whose
       route has query slots (PARAM_UNRESOLVED artifact); smoke now drives
       each task's real call_sequence.
    3. Fingerprint canonicalization: httpbin /get embeds a per-request
       X-Amzn-Trace-Id, so its raw-body hash changes on every fetch ->
       httpbin excluded from fingerprint change detection (volatile by
       design), recorded for provenance only.
- `reachability_c7.json` — start-of-session reachability x3 + verbatim
  robots.txt quotes + restful-booker cooldown check (HTTP 418 on
  POST /booking persists after >1h natural cooldown) + clock-skew
  bookkeeping vs two independent server Date headers.
- `env_playwright_install.log` — environment setup record.

— INTEL_REPRODUCER, cycle 7, 2026-08-25

### 3.2 Benign false alarms — THE DECISIVE CLAUSE, WITH ROOT CAUSE

Raw trial labeling gave fp_A = 9/360 = 2.5% > 1% bound ⇒ INCONCLUSIVE.

**Post-hoc root-cause analysis (EXPLORATORY — never confirmatory; file
`analysis_exploratory_fp_rootcause.json`)**: ALL NINE flagged A-trials are
provably TRUE detections of PENDING MUTATIONS whose resolving transition
fell inside a LATER benign window (each record's mutation preceded the
window start; each transition also resolved that mutation in the attribution
walk). The runner's benign-trial labeling omitted the prereg §7 condition
"with no intervening/pending mutation" — an instrument labeling defect, not
arm behavior. Under the prereg's own definition fp_A = **0/360**
(Wilson upper 0.83% ≤ 1%). The mechanical verdict nevertheless STANDS:
the evaluator consumed the flawed labels, and post-outcome repair or
re-evaluation is forbidden retuning.

Corrected-labels table (exploratory only): A 0/360, B 0/360, C@f* 0/360,
F 0/360, ApS 0/360 — but **E 9/360 (2.5%) and D 7/360 (1.9%) GENUINE FPs**,
all concentrated in BN2_token_rotation windows: the injected `session`
SUBTREE survives the value-placeholder exemption (presence differs from the
sealed snapshot) ⇒ canonical divergence. Instrument taxonomy gap (presence-
vs-value exemptions), caught post-outcome; also note A's apparent immunity
rests on etag-gating sparing it any look during noise — faithful to the
joint rule, but it makes A's FP test structurally easy while E/D pay the
taxonomy gap directly.

### 3.3 Pareto (secondary), SD pool

Detection rises with budget for background arms — C 15.6%/28.1%/68.8% and
mean_T 8106→3070 across f=0.25/0.5/1.0; **F and ApS dominate C at every
budget** (F@0.25: 71.9% at one quarter of a sweep — above C@1.0's coverage
at four times the budget); ApS@0.5 is the best non-oracle mean_T (1925);
saturation visible at f=1.0 (ApS flat 26/32). Cho-G-M prior partially
confirmed: hazard-sized allocation (ApS) ≈ adaptive-F, both ≫ uniform;
the pure access-triggered candidate A sits between them.

### 3.4 Capability matrix (qualitative; held-out classes scored honestly)

- M4_enum_meaning_flip (held-out #1): canonical adjudication detects on look
  (~75% for access-driven arms; C 25%) — shape-blindness AS PREDECLARED does
  NOT extend to canonical-hash adjudication.
- M7_param_rename_shape_preserved (held-out #2): detectable-on-look (~75%)
  but MISATTRIBUTED as STALE_TTL — addressing breakage presents as content
  staleness, exactly the predeclared misattribution caveat; escalation
  vocabulary cannot name it (PARAM_UNRESOLVED unreachable without request-
  side probing).
- Escalation codes observed: SCHEMA_MISMATCH (shape changes), STALE_TTL
  (shape-preserving), HTTP_ERROR_TRANSIENT retries transient windows; no
  silent substitution anywhere (transitions only ever follow real canonical
  divergence or raw-hash moves).

### 3.5 Cost-ratio sensitivity (secondary; offline repricing of ledger rows)

Primary-contrast win direction (A<C) is stable under all four frozen price
vectors {(1,2,10),(1,3,10),(1,2,5),(1,2,20)} — recomputed win counts change
by ≤1 pair; no sign flip. (Details recomputable from ledger_rows.jsonl.)

## 4. Honest limits (travel with any citation)

1. Mechanical verdict is INCONCLUSIVE — neither success nor failure of the
   mechanism may be claimed from this run.
2. The corrected-FP counterfactual (primary passes + corrected fp_A=0 ⇒
   mapping would have reached USEFUL) is EXPLORATORY ONLY; per master-prompt
   §19 a confirmatory claim requires a NEW preregistration + fresh sealed
   schedule + untouched collection evaluated once.

# INTEL REPRODUCTION REPORT — CYCLE 1

## sgdr-state-grounded-dynamic-retrieval (SGDR, arXiv:2606.04391)

- Date: 2026-08-24. Role: Intel Reproducer (binding fiche respected; Auditor validation is a separate session).
- Preregistration (FROZEN before any condition-level observation): `intel/prereg/cycle1_sgdr_prereg.md`.
- Code: `intel/experiments/sgdr_repro/` (hashes frozen in prereg). Clean-room: implemented solely from the Scout's formula-level spec; the CC BY-SA reference repository was neither fetched nor inspected.
- Raw evidence + machine results: `results/intel/reproductions/cycle1/` (`manifest_library.json`, `manifest_contexts.json`, `executability_cache.json`, `retrieval_eval.json`, `conversion_runs.json`, `conversion_summary.json`, `summarizer_cache*.json`).

---

## 1. What was tested

Scoped claim (not the WebArena headline): in SPIDER's Graph setting, stepwise retrieval scored by
`alpha*cos(task,desc) + (1-alpha)*cos(state_summary,desc)` with pool top-M=max(3k,20) and greedy MMR (lambda=0.7)
addresses executable-correct fragments better than (A) incumbent exact `goal_sig` addressing and
(B) task-text-only embedding retrieval over identical descriptions, under paraphrased goals and shifted entry
contexts — and converts into fewer novel/exploration actions at no success regression.

Library: 12 fragments built by the UNMODIFIED incumbent cold exploration on books.toscrape / quotes.toscrape /
the-internet (all 5 cold tasks succeeded). Queries: 17 included subgoals x {literal, p1, p2} x {route, start,
distractor} contexts; ground truth = execution-based executability of every same-site fragment from every context
(211 probe records, cached and shared by all conditions).

## 2. Results

### Retrieval level (primary metric, hard slice = paraphrase OR entry-shift, correct@1)

| A_native | B_plain | B_mmr | C_a04 | C_a05 | D_random |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0/74 | 25/74 (.338) | 25/74 (.338) | **36/74 (.486)** | **36/74 (.486)** | 19/74 (.257) |

- Canonical slice sanity: A_native 13/13 (incumbent perfect in its native regime), C 13/13, B 12/13.
- Pairwise C vs strongest B on hard@1: **11 wins to 0 reversals** — strict per-query dominance.
- @3: MMR lifts both B_mmr and C to 68/74 (.919) — reranking helps recall; the state term drives the @1 gain.
- alpha=0.4 vs alpha=0.5 (paper/code discrepancy): **identical rankings everywhere** at this library scale.
- All 11 C-only wins are state-discrimination cases (e.g., "run the second demonstration" from the examples menu;
  login/pager fragments addressed from shifted pages where task text alone is ambiguous or misleading).

### Downstream conversion (identical incumbent policy; only fragment lookup swapped; library writes disabled for all)

| slice | condition | novel actions (total) | subgoal success | reuse fraction |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| literal (A has native IDs) | A_native | 21 | .900 | .696 |
| literal | B_mmr | 42 | .900 | .641 |
| literal | C_a04/a05 | **39** | .900 | .698 |
| paraphrase p1 (NL consumers; A=0 retrievals) | A_zero | 400 | .600 | .000 |
| paraphrase p1 | B_mmr | 42 | .800 | .650 |
| paraphrase p1 | C_a04/a05 | **36** | **.900** | **.660** |

Cost accounting: state summarizer = deterministic adaptation (no LLM key in environment); would-be LLM calls =
11 for 49 distinct collection contexts + 2 during first conversion pass, then hash-cache makes marginal cost ~0
(mirrors reference SHA256-content-hash caching).

## 3. Frozen-rule verdict

Rule as written (combined conversion aggregate):
1. R1h(C)=36 > R1h(B_mmr)=25 > R1h(A)=0 — strictly ✓
2. Succ(C)=45/50=.90 >= max(.86, .78) ✓
3. Novel(C)=75 < min(Novel(A)=421, Novel(B_mmr)=84) ✓

**Proposed verdict: REPRODUCED_USEFUL**, claim tier ceiling PROOF OF CONCEPT.

### Ambiguity disclosure (recorded, not silently resolved)

The rule did not pin aggregation granularity. Under the STRICTEST per-slice reading, clause 3 fails on the
literal slice: with hand-authored sigs available, incumbent exact addressing remains more action-efficient
(21 vs 39 novel). The mechanism's operational advantage over the incumbent therefore exists exactly and only
in the natural-language-consumer regime — which is the regime SGDR targets and constitution §11 demands
("a future consumer must not need an internal fragment ID"). Against the like-for-like strongest baseline
B_mmr (same embedder, same MMR machinery, minus the state term), C wins on BOTH slices: fewer novel actions
(36<42, 39<42), higher or equal success (.90 vs .80 paraphrase; .90 = .90 literal), plus zero-reversal
retrieval dominance. The verdict follows the preregistered rule as written; the caveat is material and travels
with any downstream claim.

## 4. Validity gates and deviations log

- V1-V6 all pass as frozen (single embedder; hashlib-only scoring path; seeds 20260824 family; condition-independent
  cached ground truth; exclusions uniform and counted: 5 already-satisfied, 2 route-invalid contexts, 4 invalid probes,
  unsatisfiable qids excluded identically for all conditions).
- Collection-stage bugfixes, all PRE-condition-ranking except #3/#4 which occurred when conversion had produced ZERO
  usable rows; none touched rankings, metrics, or the frozen evaluation:
  1. probes stage missing `_frags` scope (crash);
  2. static precondition wrongly required all fragment steps resolvable in the ENTRY snapshot — broke cross-page
     procedures (login flows); replaced by incumbent step-by-step replay semantics; full probe re-collection;
  3. conversion pointed at nonexistent DB filename (crashed with no rows produced);
  4. goal-text builder KeyError on subgoals excluded by the frozen inclusion rule; fixed with public-keywords fallback,
     symmetric across conditions; conversion fully rerun (60/60 clean).
- No tuning of mechanisms, metrics, or success rules occurred after any outcome was visible.

## 5. Honest limits

1. Lexical-hash embedder regime (neural embedder unavailable offline); absolute numbers may differ with real embeddings;
   the C-vs-B contrast is internally controlled by design but the effect size is not transferable untested.
2. Deterministic summarizer replaces the reference LLM summarizer (contract-faithful page-kind + enabled-action-verb
   vocabulary, hash-cached, stub fallback); an LLM summarizer could produce different summary texts.
3. Small scripted-policy setting: 12 fragments, 3 sandbox sites, 10 subgoal types, heuristic agents; tiny n; no
   uncertainty intervals warranted; correlated queries within subgoals.
4. Same-site reuse only — cross-site/cross-domain transfer untested here AND untested by SGDR's authors.
5. WebArena headline numbers (37.5%/24.3% vs AWM/ASI/CER) were NOT reproduced — out of scope by prereg.
6. Insert-time dedup, sliding-window induction, verification prompts: not reproduced (out of isolation scope).
7. Mechanical descriptions are weak keys for some clusters (books travel/open-first/paginate stay unsolved at hard@1
   for ALL text conditions) — description quality, not fusion mechanism, is the binding constraint there.

## 6. Suggested next questions (for Intel Director / Graph lane)

- Does the state-grounding advantage survive a neural embedder and an LLM summarizer (the two disclosed adaptations)?
- Does fused retrieval still win when the fragment library is 10x larger (MMR/top-M become load-bearing)?
- Can mechanically-derived descriptions be upgraded without hand-authoring (the residual failure mode found here)?

The rule did not pin aggregation granularity. Under the STRICTEST per-slice reading, clause 3 fails on the
literal slice: with hand-authored sigs available, incumbent exact addressing remains more action-efficient
(21 vs 39 novel). The mechanism's operational advantage over the incumbent therefore exists exactly and only
in the natural-language-consumer regime — which is the regime SGDR targets and constitution §11 demands

(36<42, 39<42), higher or equal success (.90 vs .80 paraphrase; .90 = .90 literal), plus zero-reversal
retrieval dominance. The verdict follows the preregistered rule as written; the caveat is material and travels

   vocabulary, hash-cached, stub fallback); an LLM summarizer could produce different summary texts.
3. Small scripted-policy setting: 12 fragments, 3 sandbox sites, 10 subgoal types, heuristic agents; tiny n; no
   uncertainty intervals warranted; correlated queries within subgoals.
4. Same-site reuse only — cross-site/cross-domain transfer untested here AND untested by SGDR's authors.
5. WebArena headline numbers (37.5%/24.3% vs AWM/ASI/CER) were NOT reproduced — out of scope by prereg.
6. Insert-time dedup, sliding-window induction, verification prompts: not reproduced (out of isolation scope).
7. Mechanical descriptions are weak keys for some clusters (books travel/open-first/paginate stay unsolved at hard@1
   for ALL text conditions) — description quality, not fusion mechanism, is the binding constraint there.

- Preregistration: `intel/prereg/cycle5_unbrowse_ladder_prereg.md` — design FROZEN before any condition-level observation; frozen implementation hash table matches committed code **11/11**. Unchanged by this repair round.
- Object of repair: audit gate `results/intel/audit/CYCLE_32861355080_INTEL_GATE.json` (INTEL_AUDITOR run 32861355080, repair round 0): **REVISE / mechanism_status VALIDATED_USEFUL**, required fixes RF-1..RF-4, all documentary. This report is RF-1. The measurement was not re-run, re-tuned or altered; frozen code, data and results under `intel/experiments/unbrowse_ladder_repro/` and `results/intel/reproductions/cycle5/` are byte-identical to the audited round-0 snapshot (proof in §11).
- Verdict proposed: **REPRODUCED_USEFUL** (per the preregistered decision rule, evaluated exactly once in round 0). Claim tier ceiling: **PROOF OF CONCEPT**.

---

## 1. Mechanism identity and claim under test

The mechanism replaces repeated browser work with direct first-party-API calls via a three-tier ladder:

1. CAPTURE network traffic during real task completion;
2. FILTER responses to first-party JSON/XML candidates (content-type + origin heuristics; POST/PUT/PATCH as strong API signals);
3. EXTRACT + PARAMETERIZE endpoints into pointer-like route records (URL templates with `{param}` slots, method, required headers/auth-material association, response-shape sketch) — an index of pointers, never content;
4. RESOLVE at query time: local cache (24 h TTL) → live capture → structured HTML extraction (shared-graph vector-search tier omitted here — see §2);
5. INVALIDATE: freshness decay/TTL, lifecycle state;
6. FALLBACK RULE (safety core): stale/failed replay escalates transparently to the next tier with explicit structured codes (`REPLAY_OK / STALE_TTL / AUTH_FAIL / HTTP_ERROR / SCHEMA_MISMATCH / NO_ROUTE / PARAM_UNRESOLVED / ESCALATED_BROWSER / ESCALATED_HTML_TIER`); replay never silently substitutes for required live traversal.

Scoped claim tested here (NOT the vendor's 94-domain headline — §7):

> In SPIDER-relevant sandbox settings, a clean-room capture→extract→parameterize→replay ladder (a) discovers replayable first-party-JSON routes passively from genuine browser task completion; (b) completes repeat tasks by direct HTTP replay at materially lower wall-clock and browser-action cost than full scripted browser traversal at output equivalence; (c) honors the no-silent-substitution rule under forced staleness, authentication failure and real server-side mutation; and (d) honestly classifies server-rendered no-API targets where no qualifying route exists, falling back without silent substitution.

## 2. Faithful reproduction vs labeled SPIDER adaptations

Disposition table from prereg §2 (frozen), reproduced here for Director consumption:

| Element | Status | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Capture traffic during task completion | FAITHFUL | Playwright Chromium response recording during scripted task passes |
| Filter heuristics | FAITHFUL (paper §2 level) | first-party origin check; content-type JSON/XML; static-asset exclusion; POST/PUT/PATCH strong signals |
| Extract + parameterize into pointer-like route records | FAITHFUL | URL-template induction, query-param capture, form-body templating, auth-header association (values kept local), top-level response-shape sketch |
| Local cache with TTL, disk-persisted | FAITHFUL | 24 h freshness honored at resolve time |
| Ladder tiers | ADAPTATION (disclosed) | shared-route-graph vector-search tier omitted (private backend); local ladder is cache → live capture → HTML extraction; ranking weights therefore untested |
| Replay as direct HTTP with parameter substitution | FAITHFUL | urllib-based; captured cookie/session material applied |
| No-silent-substitution + structured codes | FAITHFUL (code vocabulary ours) | nine-code vocabulary listed in §1 |
| Validate-before-replay precondition | ADAPTATION (design donor disclosed) | Stagehand ActCache-style freshness + parameter-resolvability check incorporated conceptually; no Stagehand source viewed |
| Scripted policies instead of LLM agents | ADAPTATION (disclosed) | no LLM exists in this environment; token cost structurally zero in ALL conditions; cost axes are wall-clock + browser actions + HTTP transactions |
| Role-3 discovery input | ADAPTATION (forced by verified environment change, prereg §8) | restful-booker's booking UI was removed from the live deployment before the cycle; its API remains public. Probe-substrate capture therefore runs over scripted direct-HTTP agent work (a sanctioned SPIDER execution mode), exercising filter/extract/auth/template mechanics but not passive-UI capture (which Role 1 covers). No A-vs-B latency claim on this substrate |
| HTML-extraction recipes for no-API targets | ADAPTATION (disclosed) | hand-authored recipes ARE the mechanism's declared final fallback tier for sites with no qualifying API route |

Clean-room statement: implemented only from the Scout mechanism description plus public sandbox-site documentation (httpbin.org's own docs; restful-booker's bundled `/apidoc`). Licensing permits this path (client MIT, paper CC BY 4.0); nothing was copied.

## 3. Frozen design snapshot

- Targets/roles (prereg §3): ROLE 1 API-tier matched-pass slice = T_BIN_FORM and T_BIN_COOKIE on httpbin.org; ROLE 2 no-API classification slice = quotes.toscrape login+extract and books.toscrape category extract; ROLE 3 restful-booker probe substrate (no latency claim).
- Conditions (Role 1 only): **A** full scripted browser traversal (`goto(load)` + `networkidle` capped at 6 s; targeted-selector extraction both arms); **B** route replay from the store built during ONE discovery pass identical to A with traffic recording; **C** bare-HTTP null using publicly documented endpoints only (knowledge-privileged by construction).
- Protocol: 1 unmeasured warmup per arm per task, then K=5 measured passes per arm interleaved A,B,…; C block afterward; ≥2 s pacing between passes OUTSIDE all timed regions; single clock `time.perf_counter()` around full task execution for all arms; server timings never enter headline numbers.
- Validity gates V1–V8 (prereg §6) incl.: no artificial waits inside timed regions (V1); matched passes/exclusions arm-blind (V3); B must demonstrably work from CAPTURED traffic alone with no doc-derived hints (V4); hashlib-only hashing (V5); no tuning after first condition-level observation (V6); independent event-log checker for fallback compliance (V7); compact manifests, ≤512-byte body samples only, pointer-only store (V8).

## 5. Role-2 no-API tier: classification and fallback correctness (reliability datum)

This is the "report section 5" referenced by `decision_rule.json` clause 4. Both server-rendered targets produced ZERO qualifying routes (the filter correctly rejected HTML-only traffic, including the quotes login POST redirect) and the ladder escalated to the hand-authored HTML-extraction tier with provenance tagged:

- **T_BOO_CATEGORY_EXTRACT (books.toscrape)**: escalation succeeded — final code REPLAY_OK, provenance `escalated_html_tier:NO_ROUTE`, payload correct (≥1 title extracted). Browser arm completed with 2 actions; report-only html-tier wall 131.5 ms (no latency claim on this slice).
- **T_QUO_LOGIN_EXTRACT (quotes.toscrape)**: **the fallback itself FAILED in-run** — after correct `NO_ROUTE` detection and html-tier escalation (provenance `escalated_html_tier:NO_ROUTE`), the login+extract recipe ended in **SCHEMA_MISMATCH**; nothing was presented as success (`b_payload_ok: false`). Browser arm completed with 4 actions and a valid payload, so the failure is confined to the fallback recipe. This is recorded as an explicit **reliability datum**: the HTML tier can fail on schema drift/mismatch, and when it does, the system surfaces a structured code rather than substituting silently. Per the round-0 decision-rule record, the same html-tier code path succeeds in isolation outside the measured run — i.e., the in-run failure reflects recipe fragility on that flow, not a broken escalation mechanism. No code changes were made post-outcomes (V6); the fragility stands as an honest limitation.

Classification honesty: the mechanism correctly did NOT fabricate routes where none qualify — the expected-zero-routes prediction held 2/2.

## 6. Lifecycle probes P1–P4 and the structural no-substitution check

From `probe_events.json` (+ `role3_routestore.json`, `role3_traffic_manifest.json`), each verified by the independent event-stream checker:

- **P1 parameterization**: the induced `GET /booking/{id}` template replayed two NEW bookings created post-discovery (ids 3081, 3084) field-equal to direct-API ground truth — template slots are induced, not memorized.
- **P2 auth staleness**: replay with corrupted Basic credential returned structured **AUTH_FAIL** (HTTP 403) with nothing presented; positive control round-tripped a sentinel set→restore via valid credentials (REPLAY_OK, confirmed).
- **P3 TTL expiry**: rewinding freshness −48 h made resolve refuse with **STALE_TTL** (age 172800.5 s > 24 h TTL) and escalate rather than replay. Implementation-behavior probe of OUR compliance with the mechanism's own TTL rule.
- **P4 mutation consistency**: scratch booking (id 3080) deleted via direct API (201) → replay surfaced **HTTP_ERROR** → escalation confirmed absence (404) → final output carried provenance `escalated_html_tier:HTTP_ERROR`.
- **Pointer-only store**: mechanical structural check — no response bodies anywhere in the store (`routestore_snapshot.json`, `role3_routestore.json`); silent cached substitution is impossible BY DESIGN and verified.

Checker caveat (disclosed, non-blocking): the checker's `taxonomy_violations` counters are initialized to zero rather than derived by aggregation; they are cosmetic bookkeeping. Functionally the taxonomy is covered because each executed probe's check flips on its corresponding violation class (stale_silent ⇒ P3 would read REPLAY_OK; wrong_data_presented_live ⇒ success code without confirmation; missing_code ⇒ escalation without a code; unreported_substitution ⇒ fallback output without provenance tag). Disclosed in prose per RF-4/V6; no post-outcome code edits.

## 8. Disclosed non-design findings from round 0 (documentary only)

Per RF-4 none of these were fixed in code post-outcomes; they travel with the record:

1. **Role-3 intent-inheritance labeling artifact.** Only `/auth` and `/booking` had exact intent mappings at capture (`rsb.authenticate`, `rsb.list_bookings`); prefix-based inheritance then labeled ALL other learned routes — including create (`POST /booking`) and update (`PUT /booking/{id}`) — with intent `rsb.list_bookings` (visible in `role3_routestore.json`). No metric impact: P1–P4 select routes by method + template slots and Role-1 resolution uses exact intents; but it is honest evidence that naive intent assignment degrades beyond the exact-match regime — relevant to any future semantic-addressing integration.

## 9. Honest caveats and limitations

- **Single-host API tier**: restful-booker's UI removal (live-verified during calibration AND re-verified by the auditor) shrank the matched-latency slice to one host (httpbin.org, two flows). This limitation travels in ALL wording.
- **Attestation-based freeze timing**: the round-0 snapshot is a single commit; git alone cannot prove prereg-before-outcome ordering. Mitigations: frozen hash table matches committed code 11/11; internal event timestamps cohere physically (~93 s across discovery → checks → 30 measured passes → probes, consistent with ≥2 s pacing); pre-collection Revisions 1–2 logged with environment-fact reasons the auditor re-verified live.
- **Scripted policies, no LLM agents**: tokens structurally zero everywhere; operational-value axes are wall-clock, browser actions, HTTP transactions. n=5 measured passes per arm per task.
- **Browser-process amortization**: launched once per arm-block per task with fresh contexts per pass (identically for discovery and A passes) — disclosed; page-level costs remain inside timers; context creation sits OUTSIDE A's timer, which if anything favors A (conservative direction).
- **C knowledge privilege** (§4): parity-without-privileged-knowledge is the only abstraction value claimable on latency; template reuse on unseen records (P1) is the second demonstrated value axis.
- **Untested mechanism components**: shared-graph ranking/drift detection, marketplace semantics, x402 economics, production/anti-bot-walled behavior, schema-drift detection under real drift-inducing mutations.
- **Quotes html-tier fragility** (§5): the fallback can fail; it failed once in-run, honestly.
- Claim ceiling **PROOF OF CONCEPT** regardless of outcome (prereg §5).

## 10. Verdict proposed and maximum defensible wording

Verdict proposed: **REPRODUCED_USEFUL** — every clause of the preregistered rule evaluated exactly once passed; measurement survived full adversarial recomputation and confounder attack in the round-0 audit (gate: VALIDATED_USEFUL).

Strongest defensible wording (verbatim equal to the binding gate text, `CYCLE_32861355080_INTEL_GATE.json.maximum_defensible_wording`):

In a preregistered clean-room reproduction on public sandbox targets (scripted policies, no LLM agents), a three-tier capture->extract->parameterize->replay route ladder learned replayable first-party-JSON routes passively during genuine scripted browser task completion on both API-tier tasks (httpbin.org form submission and cookie-state read; discovery 2/2 with output equivalence at discovery time) and completed repeat tasks by direct HTTP replay with zero browser actions at 100% output equivalence, at median wall-clock speedups of 37.05x and 8.66x vs full scripted browser traversal under a realistic network-idle load policy (10/10 interleaved paired wins, 5 measured passes per arm per task, warmups excluded, 0 exclusions). Bare HTTP with perfect public-doc knowledge ran at parity or slightly faster than replay (median C/B ratios 0.92 and 0.73), so NO latency advantage over raw HTTP may be claimed; the demonstrated value of the route abstraction is reaching parity without privileged endpoint knowledge plus parameter-template generalization to unseen records (P1: induced {id} template replayed two newly created bookings field-equal to direct-API ground truth). The no-silent-substitution core held under forced stress: corrupted-auth replay returned structured AUTH_FAIL with no output presented (positive control round-tripped), past-TTL replay refused with STALE_TTL, deleted-record replay surfaced HTTP_ERROR with escalated provenance confirming absence, and the store is structurally pointer-only (no cached response bodies). On server-rendered no-API targets the ladder correctly found zero qualifying routes and escalated to a hand-authored HTML-extraction tier (books.toscrape payload correct; on quotes.toscrape the fallback itself failed in-run with SCHEMA_MISMATCH surfaced honestly - a reliability datum, no substitution occurred). Evidence tier: PROOF OF CONCEPT. Not established: the vendor's 94-domain 950ms-vs-3404ms headline (untested here; remains OFFICIAL_CLAIM with prior forensic qualifications and zero independently confirmable citations as of audit time), any multi-host API-tier result (single-host httpbin slice after a live-verified environment change removed the planned second host's UI), shared-route-graph ranking, schema-drift detection, LLM-agent operation, token costs, or production/anti-bot-walled behavior.

Forbidden wordings (binding, from the same gate):
- GENERALIZATION language of any kind;
- citing sandbox speedups (37×/8.7×) alongside or as support for the vendor's 94-domain 3.6×/5.4× or 100× marketing claims;
- any claim that route replay beats raw HTTP calls on latency (C is faster or equal here);
- any claim that the quotes.toscrape fallback succeeded;
- "first independent evaluation" stated as fact rather than as unconfirmable-at-audit-time citation-graph status.

## 4. What the valid measurement shows (clause-scoped wording only)

### 4.1 Multi-host capture->extract->parameterize->replay works (C1 PASS)

All four host-tasks — httpbin form POST, httpbin cookie flow,
petstore query-API find, demoblaze spec-less session-token SPA cart flow —
completed genuine browser discovery twice, yielded non-empty route stores
(1/1/2/7 routes), and replayed REPLAY_OK at acceptance-equivalence at
discovery time. This extends the cycle-5 single-host PoC *mechanism
reach* to four heterogeneous host-tasks including the pivotal spec-less
session-token SPA cell, within THIS RUN's scripted sandbox scope.

### 4.2 Replay economics: every per-task preregistered gate passed;
the frozen family gate failed (C2 FAIL — mechanical)

Per-task (n=5 interleaved valid pairs each, warmups excluded, B actions=0,
B equivalence on ALL pairs):

| Task | median A ms | median B ms | speedup | BCa log-ratio CI | wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T_HTTPBIN_FORM | 795.4 | 224.7 | 3.54x | [0.639, 1.315] | 5/5 |
| T_HTTPBIN_COOKIE | 616.6 | 231.5 | 2.66x | [0.957, 1.061] | 5/5 |
| T_PETSTORE_FIND | 2531.5 | 331.3 | 7.64x | [2.008, 2.050] | 5/5 |
| T_DEMOBLAZE_CART | 7133.0 | 341.3 | 20.90x | [2.889, 3.080] | 5/5 |

Leave-one-host-out direction stable in all three exclusions (10/10 and
15/15 paired wins each).

The frozen family gate required all four Holm-adjusted sign-test
p-values < 0.05; raw p = 0.03125 everywhere adjusted to 0.125 => FAIL.

POST-HOC DESIGN OBSERVATION (exploratory; NOT a rule change, NOT evidence):
at n=5 pairs the smallest achievable one-sided sign p is 1/32 = 0.03125,
and Holm's smallest-of-four multiplier is 4, so the adjusted-p floor is
0.125 > 0.05 for ANY possible outcome. As frozen (structure inherited
identical from cycle-6 section 14), the C2 family gate had zero power at
the preregistered sample size; it could never pass. The mechanical verdict
therefore could never be REPRODUCED_USEFUL under any data this design
could produce. Disclosed because it determines what this run can and
cannot mean; the verdict stands exactly as the frozen rule computed it.

Consequently NO cross-host economics advantage claim may be made from
this run. The per-task statistics above are reported as measured
outcomes inside an INCONCLUSIVE result, under the UI-traversal-vs-direct-
HTTP-scripted-policy ceiling only.

### 2.1 Donor panel arXiv:2608.00997v2 — VERIFIED, with detail upgrades

Abstract + metadata fetched live. "Registry Descriptions Go Stale Unevenly: An 89-Day Measurement of Model Context Protocol Drift, and Why Drift-Ranked Re-Auditing Under-Covers It" (Gautam Bharti; v1 2026-08-02, v2 2026-08-04). Key confirmed numbers:
- 120 observations over **88.6 days**, **19,099 distinct servers** (registry grew 3,510 -> 18,966).
- Concentration: most-active **5% generate 61% of change events**; three-quarters of long-observed servers never change; only **11.9%** of a cohort's descriptors change within 30 days vs **35.8%** naive-compounding prediction (**~3x overestimate**, heavy-tail diagnostic).
- Sparsity: only **8.6%** of servers ever rewrite descriptions vs 24.8% for descriptors.
- Targeting limit: drift-ranked re-audit at top-5% budget catches only **~20% of previously-seen changers** in a held-out window (~27% for descriptor-drift overall) and only **~10% of ALL description changers**, despite **~4x lift** — because roughly half of changes land on NEW ARRIVALS a history ranking cannot reach.
- The paper's own policy conclusion (verbatim substance): *"The control that fits is content-binding — revalidate the moment a description's hash moves — plus a sized periodic full-catalog sweep; a drift-history ranking is at best a partial, blind-to-new-arrivals control."*
- Data/code: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21709945 (CC-BY-4.0); dataset v4 DOI 21798111; panel + figure generator + analysis code released.
- Quality datum: **v2 corrected five of its own claims by re-running against its deposited artifact**; concentration/survival/targeting findings unchanged. Positive donor-hygiene signal.

### 2.2 MCP SEP-2549 caching semantics — VERIFIED live

Spec page (2026-07-28 revision) confirms: `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` REQUIRED on complete results of `server/discover`, `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/*`; `ttlMs` absent/negative -> treated as **0 = immediately stale** (safe-default posture); TTL explicitly a *freshness hint, not a polling schedule* ("Clients SHOULD NOT treat TTL as a polling interval... Implementations that do choose to poll MUST apply jitter and backoff"); notifications invalidate mid-TTL; clients MAY serve stale when refetch fails; cache key = method + parameters; per-page TTL for paginated lists. The 24h TS-SDK `MAX_CACHE_TTL_MS` cap remains anchored at its cycle-8 evidence tier. Consequence for the mission: fixed-24h-TTL arm B sits exactly at the protocol's interoperability ceiling, and the protocol itself treats declared TTL as a backstop behind push invalidation — matching the candidate's design trichotomy (pull-TTL / push-subscribe / pull-hash).

### 2.3 hermes-agent #72560 stale-catalog incident — VERIFIED live

Issue fetched live: opened **2026-07-27**, OPEN, P2, fix PR #72578 open. Root cause verified verbatim: `refresh_agent_mcp_tools()` computes ONLY `{t["function"]["name"]}` and short-circuits when the model-facing name set is unchanged — so MCP-to-MCP catalog/schema changes leave the embedded bridge catalog stale (split-brain between live registry and advertised catalog). Fix proposals converge on **byte-stable schemas OR canonical full-schema fingerprints/deep comparison**. Live negative exemplar pinning a hard requirement for the candidate: the record hash must cover FULL record content (schema/body sketch/auth association), not identity keys alone. Companion lesson from #67781 (cycle-8 record, unchanged): tombstone atomicity — refuse resurrection on ANY present/incomplete terminal marker.

## 4. Landscape broadening — new actors/mechanisms beyond the known set

### 4.1 Deep prior-art base for freshness control (novelty-bounding, decision-shaping)

- **Cho & Garcia-Molina, TODS 28(4) 2003 "Effective Page Refresh Policies for Web Crawlers"** (+ VLDB 2000 incremental crawler; TOIT 2003 frequency estimation): Poisson change models; resource-allocation result that **UNIFORM allocation always beats PROPORTIONAL allocation under binary freshness** (and under continuous decay and age metrics); their optimal policy beats both as change rates rise. Fetched live. **This is a genuine falsification risk for the sized-sweep component** and must enter the preregistered expectation-setting: the allocation question is only decidable once the objective metric is pinned (binary freshness vs integrated staleness exposure vs impatience weighting).
- Older lineage mapped by the benchmark critic: on-access conditional validation ≈ piggyback validation (Krishnamurthy & Wills, USITS 1997); adaptive per-record TTLs ≈ Douglis et al. 1997/98; declared-TTL arms ≈ cache leases (Gray & Cheriton 1989; Duvvuri et al.); B-arm ≈ dbt source-freshness `warn_after`/`error_after` (shipped calendar-TTL practice); build systems solved hash-vs-timestamp trigger selection decades ago (SCons `Decider('MD5')` vs `'timestamp-newer'`; Bazel action-cache input digests; Nix content addressing). HTTP conditional requests (RFC 9111 validators) are the deployed cheap-probe primitive the joint etag+hash rule extends.
- **Commodity data-infra prior art**: LangChain indexing RecordManager (doc hash + write-time + source-id; cleanup modes incl. full/incremental/scoped reconciliation sweeps) — hash-keyed incremental reindex + sweep is standard RAG-infrastructure practice. Implication: SPIDER's defensible residual novelty is route/capsule-specific semantics (canonicalization/volatility classes against REAL benign variation; escalation-taxonomy interaction; capsule-consumable validation objects), NOT "hash-triggered incremental recomputation works".

### 4.2 New actor: SkillGuard + DriftBench (arXiv:2605.10990) — closest competitor class found this cycle

VERIFIED live (abstract fetched; submitted 2026-05-09; Renmin U + KAUST). "Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries": extracts **role-bearing executable environment contracts** from skill documents at ingestion; validates only operational contracts against known-drift events or live conditions. Headline numbers (paper tier): contract-free CI probes produce **40% false positives**; SkillGuard raises **zero false alarms over 599 no-drift and hard-negative cases** (Wilson [0, 0.6]%); known-drift verification 100% precision / 76% recall; pre-registered study over 49 real skills finds live drift at 86% conservative precision; violated-contract localization improves one-round repair 10% -> **78%**. Ships **DriftBench**, an 880-pair skill-degradation benchmark including 107 LLM-free real-world drifts and 250 semantic hard negatives (value changes that do NOT violate role-bearing contracts).

Materiality to SPIDER: (a) it is measured evidence that **role-blind change-triggered monitoring carries large FP rates on realistic mutation mixes** — the exact trap a raw hash-move detector risks; (b) its negative-control methodology overlaps and can inform the replica benign-corpus design; (c) it proposes NO scheduling policy (no TTL/equal-budget comparison), so it complements rather than dominates the selected mechanism. Design consequence folded into §6: a relevance/role gate belongs BETWEEN hash-move detection and revalidation spend, and the benign-FP bound needs its own power arithmetic.

### 4.3 Registry/platform freshness mechanics (new specifics)

- **Official MCP registry lifecycle-status endpoints**: PR #893 "Publisher-managed deleted support" **verified merged 2026-02-27T17:00:08Z via GitHub API** (PATCH status endpoints, active|deprecated|deleted, statusChangedAt). `updated_since` incremental sync (PR #374, reported 2025-09-08) with `include_deleted` AUTO-FORCED TRUE under `updated_since` (consultation-reported at commit level; direct read pending) — i.e., the ecosystem-standard sync primitive is a **clock cursor + publisher tombstones**, not content-hash-bound. Names the calendar-cursor baseline class for any future registry-facing work.
- **PulseMCP Sub-Registry API**: recommends 24h sync cadence, states "not currently offering a 24/7 SLA" (vendor docs) — de-facto calendar-TTL mirroring, no aliveness SLA. Smithery reportedly hashes the tools array and flags "tool surface drift" plus weekly re-crawls (third-party guide claim; UNVERIFIED in code — flagged, do not cite as code fact).
- **MCP resource subscriptions** (push invalidation): `resources/subscribe` -> `notifications/resources/updated` since the 2025-03-26 revision; generalized `subscriptions/listen` with filters in the 2026-07-28 revision (consultation-reported). Client-side pattern example: openai/codex issue #16159 per-server resource cache invalidated on update events (consultation-reported, code-visible there). Spec guidance itself concedes notifications are lossy -> periodic fallback required — supports the sweep component's existence but demotes pure-push designs.
- **SeenRelay** (`github.com/ovladon/seenrelay`) — VERIFIED via GitHub API: created **2026-08-24**, pushed 2026-08-26T09:24Z, 0 stars, license NOASSERTION. Self-description: "Cooperative freshness infrastructure for AI agents" — shared cache for **freshness EVIDENCE rather than content**, so a later agent avoids repeating validation another agent already performed on the same source-backed fact. **New mechanism class**: cross-agent amortization of validation work. If pooled observations are legitimate, audit-budget accounting becomes fleet-level rather than per-store. Extremely early-stage; ideas-only watch; NOASSERTION license bars any code use.
- **TrueFoundry gateway pattern upgraded** (consultation live-verified): `cached_tool_schema` + `cached_schema_at` + `listChanged` fast-path + **drift-sized periodic sweeper** ("low single-digit minutes for active servers, longer for known-quiet") — production precedent that allocation-by-drift is shipping outside SPIDER. IBM Context Forge #1910 cited as fetch-once-never-refresh negative exemplar.
- **AgentSpan** (`oxbshw/Agent-Span`, MIT, Rust, 42 stars): agent-serving gateway storing ETag/Last-Modified per channel response, revalidating with If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since, plus FNV-1a + 64-bit SimHash fingerprinting framed as "did this meaningfully change" — cheap-signal donor adjacent to the benign-noise problem.
- **oasdiff** (Apache-2.0, active): 514-rule breaking-change catalog, CI merge-gate mode, hosted approve/reject review, and an **MCP server** exposing diff to assistants — canonical OSS spec-diff-as-CI-gate anchor.
- Market-grade uniform-polling comparator class (CODE_VERIFIED surface): **changedetection.io** (per-watch recheck intervals + schedules + June-2026 AI diff-vs-intent FP suppression) and **urlwatch** (cron + filtered-snapshot diff) — these are what arm C looks like in production.
- Methodology donor: **Dynamic Agent Skills lifecycle survey (arXiv:2607.10113, TMLR)** — maintenance-stage reporting checklist (maintenance-off ablation, operator velocities, usage-vs-utility separation) worth adopting in the prereg's reporting plan. Adjacent indexed pointers: SkillFlow-Bench (code public), ProcMEM (ICML 2026, score-based maintenance).

Folded tighteners (consolidated; full text preserved in consultation transcripts):

- **T1/F9 (baselines)**: The incumbent ladder's ACTUAL policy is lazy on-use validation via structured escalation codes (zero background budget; staleness surfaces at use). Add **on-use-reactive escalation as a co-primary baseline** and judge eager schemes on TOTAL cost (background audit + stale-use cost), not on inter-eager comparisons alone. Also add a published **adaptive-TTL estimator arm** (Douglis-style age-based TTL or Cho–G-M Poisson MLE driving per-record intervals) — if content-binding beats B/C but loses to published adaptive-TTL heuristics, the contribution collapses to packaging.
- **T2 (allocation demotion)**: Demote the drift-sized sweep from co-primary to a secondary attribution factor under a PREDECLARED exposure-integral/impatience objective; register Cho–Garcia-Molina (uniform >= proportional under binary freshness) as the falsification prior. The donor panel's transferable finding is narrow: ~50% of change mass hits new arrivals => a zero-exploration ranking provably misses half the events => any ranked allocator needs a preregistered exploration floor.
- **T3/F1 (oracle-free latency)**: Detection must be observable only at simulated probe/observation events under a preregistered budget unit; otherwise "hash-move revalidation" silently becomes an oracle that knows the sealed schedule. All arms share seeded access/jitter streams and ONE common adjudicator predicate: *first post-mutation observation after which the stored copy diverges from the sealed pre-mutation snapshot* (same normalization, same comparator code path). Arms may differ ONLY in allocation/gating policy — everything else byte-identical. Violation = MEASUREMENT_INVALID precondition stated verbatim in the prereg.
- **T4/F2/F4 (metric + budget)**: Primary = truncated-mean audit-unit latency E[min(T,H)] over a credit ledger charging EVERY observation (including access-triggered ones; c0 local compare < c1 conditional revalidation < c2 full refetch+canonicalize+diff; bookkeeping never free); detection-vs-budget Pareto grid (e.g., f x {0.25, 0.5, 1.0} of one full sweep) instead of single-point parity; cost-ratio sensitivity analysis; wall-clock demoted to descriptive under one shared traffic model; integrated staleness-exposure co-secondary (serving-frame harm), separately labeled.
- **F3 (attribution factorial)**: Factorialize trigger-source (on-access hash vs scheduled) x allocation-policy so the CONTENT-BINDING claim and the SIZED-SWEEP claim are separately attributable; raw-hash-only vs joint etag+canonical-hash ablation mandatory (demoblaze/httpbin facts cut both directions).
- **F5 (leakage-free sizing)**: Schedule-blind time-normalized Gamma-Poisson hazard estimator (hits/exposure-time with recency decay), hierarchical shrinkage toward store mean, preregistered exploration floor justified ONLY by the donor new-arrival mass; blinding attestation; oracle-ranked arm permitted as labeled diagnostic upper bound, never confirmatory.
- **F6/T4b (benign corpus)**: Expand benign suite well beyond the inherited four classes: request-header echo into bodies (httpbin-class), auth/session-token rotation (interacts asymmetrically with check frequency — FP must be normalized PER CREDIT), cache-header churn, serializer/key-order/float variance, encoding/charset, redirect-chain variation, challenge interstitials, null-vs-absent toggling, transient 5xx with preregistered adjudication window. Predeclare the FP bound and size n to it (rule-of-three: n>=300 for <=1%; inherited 0/25 bounds only ~13%).
- **F7 (statistics)**: NEVER cluster-resample at 4 stores (C(4,2)=6 assignments -> minimum two-sided p = 1/3 > 0.05 forever — the cycle-7 zero-power defect class by other means). Unit = paired mutation event within store strata; event-level permutation/sign-flip inference; ONE primary contrast (candidate vs strongest null) with Holm over m<=3; effect-size anchor derived from donor concentration stats with a saturation-null caveat (effect decays to zero near one-full-sweep budget — preregister a binding regime f<=0.5); ballpark n ~40–60 induced mutation events (>=10/store) verified by Monte Carlo (>=2000 seeds x >=2 traffic regimes x binding budgets) using the evaluator's own functions, power proof printed in-prereg; schedule-placement mix (hot/cold/new-arrival) declared at seal time.
- **F8 (comparator pinning)**: Pin B/C implementations TEXTUALLY in the prereg ("incumbent 24h TTL check" is not a spec: what does B's revalidation comparator do? refetch-and-compare sees hash moves too; stale-bit-by-clock detects nothing). D-arm degeneracy behavior declared (declared ttlMs likely absent on sandbox hosts -> immediately-stale semantics).
- **F10 + blind classes**: Freeze replica captures at seal time; harness owns all subsequent deltas exclusively (ambient upstream drift of live sandbox hosts would corrupt ground truth). Keep M4 enum-meaning-flip blind AS PREDECLARED; add a SECOND held-out blind class (e.g., param rename with shape preserved, auth-scheme swap); report a capability matrix (sensor x class) qualitatively, never selectively pooled into headline means.
- **T5 (measured artifact)**: The measured object must be a RECORD-LEVEL declarative validation object — `{validator set = joint etag + canonical-form hash with volatility-class exemptions; trigger policy; staleness-state -> escalation-code mapping}` — reported as properties of that object, because those fields transfer verbatim into Capability Capsule freshness/invalidation slots. Harness-internal logic populates nothing. Include stale-cost tiering (read harm vs irreversible-write harm; hermes #67781 anchor case) to justify a risk/freshness-tier field.

## 6. Selection decision

**SELECTED (confirmed, no re-target): `content-binding-freshness-control`**, as recorded in `state/intel_candidate.json` with the amended arm structure above. Rationale summary:
1. Assigned priority-1 mission; stop-condition fallback did not fire (no outranking actor across three independent sweeps/consultations).
2. Staleness/lifecycle is THE measured differentiator left open by the closed live line (P-8/P-9/P-10); the fixed 24h TTL was its weakest validated dimension; SEP-2549 makes 24h an interoperability ceiling and missing-TTL-as-stale the safe default; hermes incidents prove cached-procedure stores go silently stale without content binding.
3. All instrumentation is proven, audited and non-live (sealed-schedule replica-mutation harness, benign-FP bounding discipline, power-proof-before-freeze arithmetic).
4. Information gain is high in BOTH directions: a positive prices the freshness layer for Runtime capsule schema; a negative (e.g., uniform-or-lazy wins at matched total cost, per the Cho–G–M risk) kills an intuitive-but-wrong control before product contamination — and the classical literature says the negative is genuinely live, which is what makes the test discriminating rather than ceremonial.
5. Honest novelty bounding travels with the handoff: the mechanism FAMILY is old (crawlers, build systems, cache validation, LangChain-style index reconciliation; registry cursors ship today); what nobody ships or measures is route/capsule-grade content-binding with real-API benign-variation canonicalization, escalation-taxonomy interaction (incl. lazy-on-use comparison), and capsule-consumable validation objects — under adversarial sealed schedules with bounded false alarms.

## 3. Mechanism extraction — content-binding freshness control

**Donor paper:** Bharti, *Registry Descriptions Go Stale Unevenly* (arXiv:2608.00997v2, 2 Aug 2026, 13pp, 1 fig). Evidence: **PAPER_EVIDENCE + CODE_VERIFIED (Zenodo deposit, CODE_VERIFIED production gate behavior)**.

| Dimension | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Problem** | Description-level findings from point-in-time registry audits go stale; drift-ranked re-auditing under-covers description rewrites. |
| **Retained object** | Registry entry + its `content_hash = SHA-256(description)` binding per verdict (server_id, content_hash, evaluated_at) — maps directly to route/capsule record with source-content hash + etag dyad. |
| **Induction** | Panel reconstructed from 120 registry snapshots; verdict store 108 obs (2026-05-30→07-28). Not ML induction — measurement panel. |
| **Retrieval/trigger** | **Content-binding:** revalidate the moment bound hash ≠ current hash. **Sized sweep:** periodic full-catalog scan at cadence C → worst-case staleness ≤C days at N/C re-screens/day (~2.7k/day weekly, ~630/day monthly for ~19k corpus). |
| **Execution** | Read-time binding check renders mismatched verdict STALE without softening failing verdict; fail-closed gate refuses snapshots >24h old; re-screen lane on existing sweep timer (live 2026-07-29). |
| **Verification oracle** | Panel regeneration + timestamp-hash identity asserts; 747/18,543 live verdicts (4.04%) bound to no-longer-published text (99.6% resolve), split 379 born-stale (51%, instrument lag) vs 368 drifted post-judgment; drift ~26/day vs panel ~20/day consistency. |
| **Freshness/invalidation** | Hash-move + sweep; `ttlMs` as ceiling; notification invalidates mid-TTL (SEP-2549). Fix for tombstone: refuse resurrection when ANY terminal marker present/incomplete. |
| **Fallback** | Fail-closed on input freshness; sweep backfills `server_id` binding guard. |
| **Transfer** | Description-revalidation finding scoped to description surface; explicitly NOT a runtime tool-poisoning signal (§7.1). |
| **Measured numbers** | Sparse: 8.6% ever rewrite description vs 24.8% descriptors; 75% of servers (≥10 intervals) never change; top 5% generate 61% of change events; 11.9% descriptors change in 30 days (naive compounding predicts 35.8% → 73% at 89 days heavy-tail overestimate); drift-ranked top-5% catches ~20% of previously-seen description changers (~10% all changers; ~27% for descriptors). Lift H1→H2: 7.1× for descriptors (4.4%→31.2%), 4.8× for descriptions (2.8%→13.8%) — predictability buys little coverage because surface sparse + half of changes on new arrivals history cannot rank. |
| **Baselines / limits** | Baseline is drift-ranked re-auditing; limit is new arrivals + sparse rewriting + reappearance channel (12 cases) + heavy-tail naive compounding trap. |
| **Licensing** | CC-BY-4.0 dataset+code; CC-BY-4.0 paper. |

**Evidence tier:** PAPER_EVIDENCE (panel findings) + CODE_VERIFIED (Zenodo regeneration) + OFFICIAL_CLAIM/CODE_VERIFIED (SEP-2549 spec) + INDEPENDENT_REPORT (hermes incident). Reproducibility is exact: every panel-derived number regenerates from deposit.

## 4. Baseline critique and prereg fixes (benchmark red-team)

**Why fixed TTL + uniform is strawman:** Uniform at matched budget automatically loses to any history-informed ranking; 24h TTL is a spec ceiling, not an optimized policy. The paper itself shows the stronger null is drift-ranked (top-5% caps at ~20%). Probe-on-use dominates under sparse reuse.

**Required strong baselines (frozen arms):**
- Fixed 24h TTL (ladder incumbent) — weak null.
- Uniform sweep at equal audit budget — weak null.
- Drift-ranked sweep without hash (paper's best history-informed policy).
- Sized sweep without hash-move (isolates trigger vs sizing).
- Probe-on-use / validate-before-replay (Stagehand ActCache pattern: revalidate only when invoked).
- HTTP orthodox conditional (`ETag + If-None-Match`, joint etag+hash applied identically to ALL arms).
- SEP-2549 `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` with missing-ttl-as-stale + notification invalidation (protocol-native, scope-aware).
- Random audit + always-revalidate ceiling.

**Design flaws fixed:**
- **Power:** Pre-freeze numeric proof from evaluator's own functions for Holm one-sided family (m = shape classes) and Wilson FP bound (require Wilson upper ≤0.05 at n≥80 clusters). History Holm zero-power lesson (n=5 ⇒ min adjusted p 0.125) must not repeat.
- **Unit of analysis:** cluster (replica-store cluster), not record; cluster BCa bootstrap.
- **Leakage:** Size sweep on panel train split, evaluate on harness test split + Paperclip/Snyk TOCTOU held-out timelines; schedule sealed, no threshold tuning on revealed schedule.
- **Metric gaming:** Per-class median latency + recall@budget + AU-budget; pooled accuracy forbidden. Benign corpus must include transport-volatile (httpbin `$.headers.*`) and CDN byte-churn under identical etag (demoblaze rule). Hash fetched at decision time, oracle hash from mutated ground truth unavailable. Tombstone guard enforced.
- **Budget:** Count hash fetches as network calls; include wall-clock if hash fetch costs.

---

## 6. Why content-binding wins on information value

1. **It populates the empty Capsule field.** V2 requires `freshness/invalidation` per capsule; today it is null. The paper supplies the first longitudinal measurement of *how* staleness concentrates and why history-ranking fails, plus a policy with plannable budget (hash-move ~20/day vs sweep N/C/day) that directly instantiates the field.

2. **It survives falsification in both directions.** If hash-move wins at bounded FP vs drift-ranked and probe-on-use, it becomes the Runtime primitive. If it loses to probe-on-use or HTTP orthodox, it kills a plausible but wasteful policy before Product contaminates the schema — high information either way.

3. **It is the cheapest discriminating test.** Replica stores + sealed-schedule mutations + Zenodo panel are all non-live with proven harness (115/115 selftest in cycle 8, 57/57 recompute in cycle 7). Harpist and WALT need new harness layers; freshness reuses existing harness.

4. **It is decision-relevant now.** SEP-2549 made 24h a standard and missing-TTL-as-stale the safe default; hermes proved tombstone non-atomicity is a production cost multiplier. Runtime cannot finalize `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` propagation without a measured staleness policy.

---

## 7. Reproduction design (minimal, prereg-frozen)

**Hypothesis:** hash-move (joint etag+hash) + sized sweep detects induced mutations faster/at lower audit budget than fixed 24h TTL and uniform sweep at equal budget — and vs drift-ranked and probe-on-use — without exceeding bounded benign FP.

**Arms (frozen, matched audit budget including hash fetches):** A hash-move+sized sweep, B fixed 24h TTL, C uniform sweep; strong comparators D drift-ranked (no hash), E sized-without-hash, F probe-on-use, G HTTP orthodox ETag, H SEP-2549 ttlMs, I random, J always-revalidate.

**Target:** per-class median detection latency, recall@budget, audit budget to 90% recall, benign FP rate.

**Sampling:** sealed schedule generation, m replica-store clusters, host-auth stratification; resampling unit = cluster.

**Holdout:** size sweep on panel train; evaluate on harness test + Paperclip/Snyk TOCTOU held-out.

**Uncertainty:** cluster BCa bootstrap + exact permutation for latency, Holm step-down family, Wilson for FP.

**Adequacy:** power proof from evaluator's own functions before freeze; synthetic five-verdict fixtures + regression lock + filename-wiring audit.

**Falsification/survival:** survive iff at bounded FP wins efficiency vs both weak and strong baselines on ≥4/5 shape classes (M4 excluded); otherwise REPRODUCED_NO_ADVANTAGE. M4 blindness replication expected.

**Constraints carried:** PROOF OF CONCEPT ceiling max; GENERALIZATION forbidden beyond replica/route-capsule scope; scout-tree figures (83.58× etc.) barred forever; cycle-9 cited only as "single guarded evaluation" with dual-collection caveat; vendor headline OFFICIAL_CLAIM forever; no further live collection for unbrowse ladder except window-2 deliverables.

Three-path execution ladder over first-party ("shadow") APIs:

| Stage | Mechanism | Tier |
|---|---|---|

**Client/server boundary (load-bearing for reproduction):** the MIT repo is the *client boundary only*. ## 3. Benchmark forensics — what survives, what does not

Recomputed from the vendor's published CSV (94 rows):

**Survives:** mean 950 ms vs 3,404 ms (ratio-of-means 3.58× ≈ "3.6×"); median per-domain speedup 5.35× ≈ "5.4×"; 94/94 wins; fastest-domain pair matches.

**Does not survive contact with the same CSV:** paper claims 18 domains <100 ms — CSV contains **7**; paper median latency 630 ms — CSV **661**; paper Playwright median 3,402 ms — CSV **2,954**; IQRs differ in both arms.

**Harness artifacts favoring the treatment arm (`run_warm_cache_bench.py`, CODE_VERIFIED):**
- baseline adds an unconditional `wait_for_timeout(2000)` to every page load — flat +2 s that accounts for most of the claimed 2,454 ms "browser overhead";
- baseline extracts raw `inner_text("body")`, contradicting the paper's stated CSS-selector targeted extraction;
- treatment arm prefers **server-reported** `timing.total_ms` over measured wall clock; baseline gets wall clock only;
- one warmup + one measured pass, vs the paper's three-pass protocol;
- every headline row is `source=marketplace` — warmed by construction, zero miss/fallback coverage in the headline table.

**Vendor's own honest negatives (OFFICIAL_CLAIM):** internal live runs report 50% coverage (9 PASS / 4 ANTIBOT_BLOCK / 5 PRODUCT_FAIL) and 0.50 retrieval coverage on an adversarial corpus with named Cloudflare/DataDome failures; protected-site median speedup 2.1× vs 6.8× unprotected; blocking sites excluded by design; Kuri Linux-x64 crashes (#50); deprecation logic unwired.

**Repo metadata inconsistencies:** description says 235 domains (paper: 94; tasks.json: 15); single push 12 days before submission; referenced result files absent; README describes a different earlier run (1.4–3.7×, "47% of failures were disambiguation issues").

**Claim-tier violations recorded:** "peer-reviewed" applied to an arXiv preprint; "18 domains under 100ms" repeated in agent-facing SKILL.md against its own CSV's 7; "30× faster" (single best domain) marketed as typical replay economics.

Song, Xu, Zhou & Neubig, *Beyond Browsing: API-Based Web Agents*, ACL 2025 Findings: with **pre-documented official APIs**, hybrid API+browsing agents beat browsing-only by >24% absolute (38.9% WebArena success). This independently supports "direct API access helps when APIs are known". It does **not** test traffic-derived discovery, sharing, staleness or fallback — precisely the part of Unbrowse still resting on vendor-run evidence. It also documents the hybrid flexibility premium (more steps/cost than pure API path).

## 4. Priority-3 runtime actors — mechanism extraction

**Stagehand (Browserbase) — deterministic caching at two granularities.** `CODE_VERIFIED`: the v4 branch contains `packages/core/lib/v3/cache/{ActCache,AgentCache,CacheStorage,serverAgentCache,utils}.ts`; ActCache key construction was read directly in source this cycle: `(sanitized instruction, normalizeUrlForCacheKey(pageUrl), sorted variable keys)`; replay validates page state via `waitForCachedSelector` (default 15s attach timeout) before executing cached actions; misses/self-heal fall back to live LLM resolution; AgentCache records whole multi-step runs for zero-LLM deterministic replay; Browserbase-hosted sessions get managed server-side caching with `cacheStatus` HIT/MISS surfaced from act()/extract(). Performance deltas (cold 15–60+s → cached 1–5s, 0 tokens) remain `OFFICIAL_CLAIM`.
→ Role in this cycle: **baseline-design donor**. At least five independent public implementations now convert captured browser traffic into declarative specs — the ladder's extraction stage is becoming a commodity:

2. **TabAPI** (`CODE_VERIFIED`, Lay4U/tabapi): record→analyze→export **OpenAPI 3.0 + TS SDK + MCP server config + replay tests**; `tabapi replay` returns pass/fail/**changed** summaries for CI drift detection.
3. **Vespasian** (`CODE_VERIFIED`, praetorian-inc/vespasian, Apache-2.0, 125★, pushed 2026-08-24): traffic/HAR/Burp import → REST/GraphQL/SOAP/gRPC spec recovery incl. **SPA bundle static extraction recovering routes no click exercises** (Next.js chunk-filename segment mining), 404-decoy filtering, byte-deterministic output.
4. **Harpist** (`CODE_VERIFIED`, kenobi-ai/harpist, MIT, 9★, pushed 2026-08-04): Chrome-recorded workflow traffic → **versioned per-host `contract-profile.json`** → derived contract.ts/openapi.json/docs; additive recordings (later sessions refresh credentials + extend endpoint set); credentialed replay + `auth check --all`; ships as an agent skill so the agent refines its own recordings. ## 4. Adjacent-system staleness-rate priors (new quantitative anchors)

- **PreAct** (arXiv:2606.17929, `PAPER_EVIDENCE`): verify-gated compiled replays for CUAs; blind linear replay showed **50–67% cache-miss rates on WebArena**; verify-before-store gate **rejected ~83% of compiles** there (brittle predicates). First published quantification of how fast naive action-level replay goes stale — the action-granularity counterpart to the route-ladder's TTL question. Also documents that gate-only without miss→fallback loses to blind caching (fallback policy is load-bearing).
- **Weblica** (arXiv:2605.06761, `PAPER_EVIDENCE`): HTTP-level record/replay for training-env construction with **auto-synthesized volatile-parameter normalization rules** (timestamps/tokens stripped from URLs/headers/bodies), rule validation by isolated playback, replay-fidelity-as-admission-criterion (15.6K of 146K tasks retained). Method donor for equivalence-canonicalization and cache-key normalization under drift.
- **Muscle-Mem** (`CODE_VERIFIED`, pig-dot-dev/muscle-mem, Apache-2.0, ~766★): behavior cache keyed by environment Checks (`capture`/`compare`); hit→deterministic trajectory replay with zero model calls; **no TTL concept at all** (pure environment-match validity) — the design gap the route ladder's natural-TTL arm probes.
- **Screen-activity compilation** (arXiv:2608.05784, `PAPER_EVIDENCE`): guarded replay plans fail safe via expected-element/role guards; introduces measured **Routine Overhead Ratio R=60–343×** and delegable recurrence h≈8%, bounding fleet-wide replay savings at h·(1−1/R)≈8% — the emerging honest-accounting frame any "replay saves X%" claim will be judged against; forbids double-counting with caching gains.

- Statistics: per-host paired log-ratio BCa bootstrap primary; mixed-effects cross-host (host random intercept, auth-tier interaction); asymmetric n permitted (replay 20–30 vs browser ≥5) with MDE predeclared; randomized block order; leave-one-host-out required (wins-concentration precedent); denominator floor (<2s browser passes reported separately); Holm on secondaries.
- Mechanical verdict rules enumerated (silent substitution anywhere ⇒ MEASUREMENT_INVALID; adjudication>10%; availability<95%; discovery below floor; cross-arm contamination; infra-coded failures>20%). REPRODUCED_USEFUL requires gate-pass ≥90% lower-bound on every qualifying host + zero invariant violations + log-ratio CI>0 with ≥half hosts individually CI>1 + spec-null failing/slower on ≥1 spec-less host (causal separation). REPRODUCED_NO_ADVANTAGE iff gates pass but spec/null parity everywhere or speedup CI includes 1.
